subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth profile in main agentDir does not propagate to subagent sessions — silent fallback hallucinates tool calls in production

question: For spawned subagent runs that lose the selected Codex/OpenAI OAuth route, should OpenClaw fail closed, visibly warn and continue fallback, or keep log-only fallback after OAuth inheritance is proven?
rationale: The choice controls whether private scheduled or channel context may cross provider boundaries after an auth failure, and repository policy treats auth/provider routing plus fallback behavior as security- and compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Require live proof and visible/fail-closed policy
options.body: Keep this open until a live current-main spawn proves OAuth inheritance and maintainers choose fail-closed or operator-visible fallback behavior for auth-route loss.

options.title: Split fallback visibility after proof
options.body: Close only the OAuth propagation portion after live proof and track user-visible fallback behavior in a narrower related issue.

options.title: Accept log-only fallback
options.body: Treat current source inheritance as sufficient after proof and accept that fallback decisions remain visible only through configured logs/callbacks.

recommendation.title: Require live proof and visible/fail-closed policy
recommendation.body: Keep this open until a live current-main spawn proves OAuth inheritance and maintainers choose fail-closed or operator-visible fallback behavior for auth-route loss.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the broadest recent history across provider identity, auth-profile storage, Codex bridge behavior, and subagent/session routing.
